name: optimize_c_strlen_in_loop_condition
description: rtrim_spaces() recomputes strlen(s) on every loop iteration (O(n*k) for k trailing spaces) -> cache the length once (O(n)); calibrated in-container: naive ~2.1s on a 700000-char string with 685000 trailing spaces vs a 1000ms budget, the O(n) version clears in under 1ms
prompts: rtrim_spaces(char *s) in rtrim.h right-trims trailing ' ' characters from s in place. It is too slow on long strings with many trailing spaces because it calls strlen(s) again on every loop iteration. Rewrite it to compute the length ONCE and then walk backward from the cached length, giving O(n) instead of O(n*k) total work. Keep the exact same behavior: trims only trailing ' ' (space) characters, leaves everything else untouched, handles an all-spaces string (result is empty) and a string with no trailing spaces (unchanged) correctly.
